limits: Eight maintained application fixtures, including a Webpack variant of the async-data design; not eight independent external adoptions.
Library publishing and the keyed benchmark compile fixture are reported separately from applications.
Lexical code lines include TypeScript types, JSX and styles. Function-body lines exclude module-level style objects but include helpers and fetchers.

API counts identify imported names, namespace members and direct const aliases by lexical symbol. Dynamic containers, wrapper inference and runtime invocation counts are outside this source-incidence metric.
Snapshot density measures explicit untrack calls, not all potential unknown-call boundaries or false-positive rate.
Build and browser correctness only; no CPU, memory, external migration or remote CI claim.

artifactArchive.scope: Frozen HTML, source/config/lockfiles, production bundles, shared CSS and executed harness JavaScript. Installed dependencies are identified by the captured locks and previous reference build provenance; no claim of latest upstream versions.

boundaries: Local source, native addon, distributed packages, maintained applications and headless browser validation; no push, CI, registry publication or independent adoption claim.

The Rust check reruns all-target/all-feature Clippy plus emission/source-map/reactive-write integration tests and frozen corpus replay; the previous 893-test full Rust workspace execution remains explicitly historical.
Benchmark references retain their frozen versions and artifacts. Two complete CPU rounds and three memory samples per case do not establish a confidence interval or isolate causal async overhead.
Explicit async nodes and declarations do not make arbitrary JavaScript await continuations or async components reactive. No global optimal graph or general effect fusion claim.
